steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Once upon a time, there was a child who was imprisoned in an old, old tower.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The script of his life had been written from the moment of his birth. Like an opera, every aria, every scene was meticulously planned, and all he could do was follow it.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: One day, the child realized that he was part of the show.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It was all a masquerade. Love, hate, resentment, everything around him was fake.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Confused, frightened, and angry, he called the score 'fate,' and tried to resist it.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: At one point, he even thought he had succeeded in escaping from the stage.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But he forgot that freedom granted by another can never be true freedom. When the threads of fate tightened again, there was nowhere for him to go except back on stage.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But this time, he chose to fight.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The show would go on. He would struggle for the benefit of the audience in the seats. Still, he thought he could at least glare back at them, and scorn the fate that they had imposed upon him.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But he often wonders... if he was still in the play, how can he tell where the stage ends, and the audience begins?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And if all of us are part of a play like he is, how would we know when it truly ends?

steps.name: Child
steps.text: Poor kid! Will he get out? Will he become a hero and defeat the bad guy?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A hero... Sadly, not everyone can be a hero. Given enough time, some heroes stop being heroes, or even become villains.

steps.name: Child
steps.text: That's not the kinda story I want to hear!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Alright, alright... let's start from even earlier in the story then. That way, we won't get to the ending you don't want to hear today.

steps.name: Child
steps.text: Nein! Hurry it up already!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You guys like playing at Forest Park, don't you?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Did you know that it wasn't actually built to commemorate the heroes who died resisting the Witch King?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Gustav Park was built to commemorate the deeds of a great ruler.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And in his story, he was a 'hero' too.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Huff... huff... hah...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Oh, so that's how it is. If it isn't my old friends.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I knew it didn't make any sense for Their Majesties to go through the trouble of bringing me back and sparing my life for a few days, only to send assassins.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: You are the key to the plan, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Yes, yes, we've all heard this one before.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Have you learned nothing from what happened with Gertrude? All that effort, and not even the ruins of a concert hall to show for it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What do you want from me this time? To blow up the park above us?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Gräfin Strollo's failure was born of ignorance. She and the original experimenters were nothing but useless rabble.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: They knew His Majesty's melody, but not how to play it properly, and foolishly sought to use it as a weapon to spread the calamity of Originium.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Such uncouth violence is an affront to art. Even if he had awakened from it, he would have sentenced them to death for their blasphemy.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ha, of course. So you're saying that Gertrude was a fraud, but you're the real deal?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then... what? You need me to appeal to Their Majesties to bestow you a medal proving your commitment to the arts?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: We seek only your understanding.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: You are His Majesty's heir, the symbol of his glory, the manifestation of his flesh and blood, and the continuation of his melody.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: We believe that you will bring glory back to Urtica, and to Leithanien.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Then do it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Take back his glory, his flesh and blood, his melody.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I wonder though... Without those, what would be left of the individual known as 'Ebenholz'?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Perhaps it is your infection, or perhaps the result of Rhodes Island's training.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: You've certainly become stronger.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: And yet... you show not even a sliver of His Majesty's strength.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: I... I must go...

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Freeze.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: What are you doing here?!

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Take another step, and I'll have you arrested.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: But I haven't—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You haven't formally joined those lunatics yet? Good for you.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: They're no lunatics! Maybe you see His Majesty's reign as one of terror, but all he did was punish the nobles who stood in the way of progress!

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Why am I not allowed to miss him? Why can't I long for a Leithanien where someone like me could become somebody?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Because I know that era better than you do.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Listen, junge. When I first came to Leithanien, I accidentally stepped on a poster on the ground.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Every other person on the street was probably a spy. I was a trader from Laterano at the time, and they planned to execute me as a 'subversive foreign element.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You could have contacted the Notarial Hall or the Seventh Tribunal.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Certainly, Reverend Executor. Just like you could have broken into the most heavily-guarded Arts jail on your own and rescued me.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But like most Sankta, your wings are ornamental, not functional.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Leithanien is more than a stone's throw from Laterano. Not even you could have helped a Liberi who was scheduled to be executed the very next day.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But you survived, and became Leithanian.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Because someone saved my life.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: A limping old Liberi, a soldier who'd killed a few Gauls in his time. He later joined the Gendarmerie, essentially the Witch King's secret police at the time.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: He took pity on me and got me out. I'm told the executioner got a fancy new cigarette case for his trouble.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Only a few days later, the Witch King executed another batch of dissidents, right here in this park.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And when I looked up from the crowd, can you guess whose face I saw among the twisted statues?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Are you scared? You should be.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Go home, junge, and don't ever get involved in these things again.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: We should go too, Reverend Executor.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You've also detected the use of Arts. Someone is fighting.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I'll let the Empresses' Voice know. Let them worry about it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We will miss our chance to apprehend the criminal.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: When will you understand? I don't want that chance.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: If I strolled into that park, I'd find a group of masked people calling themselves the 'Echoes of Herkunftshorn.'

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And Their Majesties would certainly expect me to draw my weapon and arrest or kill them.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But do you know whose faces I'd see when I removed their masks?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Perhaps the heir of a Graf, or the scion of a Kurfürst.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: As for me? If I'm lucky enough to survive, I'd be sent straight back to jail. This battle in the park? Ha! It'd go down as nothing more than a little brawl over some private grudge.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Just like Jan's sister, Yulia. I tried to catch the last bastard to see her, but couldn't touch a hair on his head because of his father's title, his family, and the Kaiserinnen's intervention!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: An enforcer of the law should act only in accordance with the law, not his own interests.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Since when has the law cared about a man's life or death?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The law allows you to leave a last will and testament. If you are killed in battle, I will see it executed to the letter.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...You have one twisted sense of humor.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But that reminds me, when I joined the uprising against the Witch King and attacked the Spire, I truly believed that I'd leave something behind, even in death.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But look at me now. An alcoholic who spends his days taking bribes and bowing to high nobles.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You're absolutely right, I'm not fit to enforce the law. I bet the old man who saved me is rolling in his grave.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The events of the past should not cloud your judgment of the present.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You could not save that girl named Yulia, but you saved her brother. And you have the chance to save someone else.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I envy you, Reverend Executor. Back when I left Laterano, I thought the Sankta were hard to understand. But now I realize that there's no one simpler.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But... are the laws of Laterano always correct?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have in fact encountered a case like the one you mentioned.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The case I am pursuing right now. It is very special to me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Her actions have seriously threatened the order of Laterano. The outcome is clearly wrong, yet she has continued to escape the law's judgment.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Do you ever feel doubt, then? Disappointment?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: In my experience, disappointment is born from having previously held strong positive feelings towards something.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Which you never had?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You're... different from the other Sankta I know. You've never loved Laterano, have you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not believe such sentiments to be necessary to perform my duties.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Maybe you're right.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Or maybe, when you're finally forced to doubt yourself, and find yourself wavering, lost, like me... you'll realize that you need a strength, a reason.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And that's when you'll discover that the law offers no guidance.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I hear a cello. The target is just ahead.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you refuse to follow, I will proceed to the suspect's location and complete the mission myself.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I would prefer to have the cooperation of the Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Not my problem. I need to head back and hand over my resignation to the city council. Don't worry, I'll pass the documents you gave me along to my successor before I leave Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not believe that the former hero is dead, Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: After all, you're standing right in front of me. Accurately determining a person's life or death is part of my job.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Seriously?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Ha.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The target isn't here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This cello tune...

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: You see the sculptures spraying water? Their Arts have been modified to reproduce her performance.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: Why are you pointing that at me, Sankta? Have you lost your mind?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Marigold Alley, Forest Park... You have been at the scene of every incident.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your behavior is abnormal for a Leithanian of your age.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The evidence provides plenty of reason to suspect you.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: And that's why you're pointing a gun at me? Did it ever occur to you that I could be on your side?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: When dealing with someone attempting to hide their identity, detention followed by interrogation is the most efficient option.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: You're even less flexible than a statue tuned by the worst caster!

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: I was wondering who this trap was for. Any Leithanian child off the street could've told you this wasn't a live performance.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: Whoever set it must know you well. She knew you'd come after the sound of a cello like a hungry tuskbeast pouncing on a piece of meat, ignoring everything else.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: Giving her an opening to approach her real target.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: That spineless Gendarmerie commander? Why bring him up?

spans.text: That spineless Gendarmerie commander? Why bring

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your assessment is correct, Arturia lured me away. It is Loris Bordin she wants.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Thiem? It's me. Is Jan back yet?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Okay, good.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Tell him I'm very sorry about his sister... about Yulia.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I'm leaving Leithanien soon. The leads I've collected over the years are in my house in Bodenshof. The key's in the wallet I gave you. Give it to Jan.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Hopefully... someone will take over the case after I'm gone.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I've been pursuing it for so long now. I couldn't get a result, but maybe someone else can.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...This is a bigger commotion than the previous ones.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Pym? I'm near Forest Park. There's a situation here. Get a team over... no, one team might not be enough. Get everyone you can.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Yeah, it's probably those masked schurken. Maybe they set fire under the asses of a pack of gloompincers in order to blow up the sewers.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Let's just hope no unlucky bastard gets caught up in the mess.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Music?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Who's there? ...A Sankta?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Reverend Executor? Is that you?

steps.name: 'Federico'
steps.text: The events of the past should not cloud your judgment of the present.

steps.name: 'Federico'
steps.text: You could not save that girl named Yulia, but you saved her brother. And you have the chance to save someone else.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...An illusion? No, just a memory.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Oh, Pym. No, it's nothing. There's only me here. It's just that I was reminded of something.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Ja, the bastards are right below me. I'll leave a beacon here.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Ja, I know, it's dangerous. I'll keep my distance.

steps.name: 'Stubborn Apprentice'
steps.text: Run away with your tail between your legs, meine Herr. Whatever courage you once had is ancient history.

steps.name: 'Stubborn Apprentice'
steps.text: 'The first soldier to set foot in the Witch King's Spire'—do you really think you're still that same hero?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Get out of my head, you asshole.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: No, I wasn't talking to you, Pym. Time to move. I'm gonna hang up.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...I know better than anyone that I'm a coward. I couldn't find out how Yulia died. Couldn't even take revenge for her.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Yulia... Yulia.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: What would you say if you saw me now?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You were always so warm and gentle. Maybe you wouldn't let your disappointment show.

steps.name: 'Gendarmerie'
steps.text: Don't hang your head, junge.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Hey there, old man. Now it's your turn to pop out of my memories, huh?

steps.name: 'Gendarmerie'
steps.text: You're not too quick on the uptake, but you've got guts. Not many could look a picture of the Witch King in the eye, let alone step on it.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I was just an unlucky bastard who happened to walk by. Was it really worth losing your life over someone like me?

steps.name: 'Gendarmerie'
steps.text: Don't feel like you owe me anything.

steps.name: 'Gendarmerie'
steps.text: Did you really think I was going to die in bed, after working for the Witch King for so many years?

steps.name: 'Gendarmerie'
steps.text: Letting you go just helped me sleep at night for once, for the last few days of my life.

steps.name: 'Gendarmerie'
steps.text: Same goes for you, junge. If you feel guilty, then try saving a few more lives before you go.
The Liberi limps away and disappears into the shadow beneath the sun.
It's a long one, like the one the Spire cast all those years ago.
Many lives faded into those shadows, with not a soul to gaze upon them. It was how things were, and how they still are.
The cello music fades away.
Only the tremors beneath his feet remain. He knows they are the sounds of innocent souls struggling for life.
He could stay put.
He could leave Leithanien like he left Laterano.
All he'd need to do is turn around and leave, like he's done for decades now. So much easier than leading the charge, no?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I'm tired, old man.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I want to live. Not just that, but to drink freshly brewed beer every day, to listen to jazz with Pym and the boys after work, and to take a trip to Sami next summer.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I... couldn't die a hero like you did.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But why...

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Why am I disappointed?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: You're tired, young Graf.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Huff... hah...

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Oripathy eats away at you. If you continue to use your Arts, only death awaits.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And... are you afraid of that?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: I fear only what we must do to stop you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Mmph—Argh!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: My... head... hurts...

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: We do not wish to harm you.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: But the Concertmaster says that the melody within you is more valuable than your mind.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: We will... put you to sleep for a while, if need be.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You want to wipe my mind...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I... won't... let...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Arrrgghhh!

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: A Liberi... in a Gendarmerie uniform?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Just one?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Trying to be a hero, are you?
'Go. My men are on their way.'
He hears the stranger say to him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Dan... ke.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Don't let him get away!
Ebenholz knows he will not get another chance.
Blood drips down from a corner of his mouth. His head is splitting.
The battle behind him continues. He wants to see the face of his hero, but the tiny silhouette is quickly engulfed in light from Arts and explosions.
All he can do is run.
He keeps running.
He knows not where this path leads, nor the effort it will take to escape its predestined end.
